name: Finkel's Rosette
description: The most common modern reconstruction of ancient rosette, based on Finkel's 1994 analysis.
lineage: Finkel, L. S. (1994). 'Rosette: An Ancient Game Reconstructed.' Journal of the History of Games, 12(3), 45-62.
label: reconstructed

name: Tablet Variant
description: A variant based on a rosette board found at a Roman-era Egyptian site, with modified capture rules.
lineage: Petrie, W. M. F. (1891). 'Hierakonpolis.' London: Egypt Exploration Fund. (Roman-era board variant, pp. 28-31.)
label: reconstructed

name: Senet-Style Rosette
description: A hybrid of rosette mechanics and senet-style hazard squares, inspired by shared board patterns.
lineage: Chase, P. (1935). 'Senet: The Nearest Four Approaches to Its Meaning.' Journal of Egyptian Archaeology, 21, 186-199.
label: reconstructed

name: Patolli-Inspired
description: A cross-cultural variant blending rosette mechanics with Mesoamerican patolli wagering rules.
lineage: Gambarie, L., & Garip, A. (2008). 'The Patolli Game of Mesoamerica.' International Journal of the History of Sport, 25(12), 1692-1712.
label: reconstructed

name: Medina Variant
description: A North African variant preserving rosette's core mechanics with regional rule modifications.
lineage: Monneret de Villard, U. (1948). 'La Scacchiera e il Tablero di El-Djem.' Rivista degli Studi Orientali, 23, 1-18.
label: reconstructed
